newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Yemen envoy meets Saudi minister on border dispute.
newsitem.headline: Yemen envoy meets Saudi minister on border dispute.

text.p: Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef and Yemeni Foreign Minister Abdul-Karim al-Iryani met on Monday and reviewed steps taken to settle a 61-year-old border row between the oil-rich kingdom and its impoverished neighbour.
The official Saudi press agency (SPA) said the talks were "within the context of continuous meetings to reach agreement on the remaining border demarcation line".

An official source in Sanaa said earlier Iryani, who is also Yemen's deputy prime minister, flew to the Red Sea city of Jeddah to arrange for a planned visit to the kingdom by Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh and discuss bilateral ties.
The official Yemeni news agency said he was carrying a letter from Saleh to King Fahd.
No date has been set for Saleh's visit.

Iryani's trip is the first high-level visit to Saudi Arabia since Saleh appointed a new government this month after April general elections, Yemen's first since a 1994 civil war nearly tore the Arab country apart.
Saleh met King Fahd last summer to speed up talks to settle the border row.
Yemen has hinted in recent months it might resort to international arbitration if more than a year of talks with Riyadh failed to settle the dispute.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before the two sides signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the dispute.
A joint committee looking into border demarcation has met scores of times since 1995.

Yemen's relations with Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, have improved in the last few years. Sanaa angered its Gulf Arab neighbours when it appeared to side with Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
